chapter: First big band, his father, arriving in Kansas City
title: First big band heard in person, with Junior Raglin and Maxwell Davis
summary: In Albuquerque he heard Gene Coy's big band, his first, with Junior 'Bear Tracks' Raglin, blues singer Blues Bailey and Maxwell Davis, and was overwhelmed.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: So now, after Eddie Hill, then you -- then what happens next?

Well, after Eddie left, then we -- Howard, the group, you know, would continue to work around Albuquerque there and then long about that time, Gene Clay came through there and I'd never -- well, I never had heard a big band, you know, just to -- that was the first big band I heard in person and Gene ________ comes through there and they was doing 'Christopher Columbus' and I heard all that brass and the reeds and the rhythm section and oh, I like to went crazy, you know?
I hadn't heard nothing like that, you know.
That was a good band, was it?
It was a good band.
Were they playing a ballroom or something?
Yes, they were playing a ballroom and so -- well, Howard and I was remarking about it, you know, and so -- Howard and I, we kind of stuck together then pretty good and, you know --
Who was in his band then? Anybody that we would know? Gene _______'s band?
Gene _______'s band? Yeah, Bear Tracks -- remember the guy that later played bass with Ellington?
What name?
We called him Bear Tracks. Junior --
Raglin.
Raglin.
Oh.
Right, right.
He was in that band.
Junior was in that band, see? And Junior was playing guitar in that band.
What did they call him Bear Tracks for?
Well, I think we called him Bear Tracks because he had big feet.
(Laughter.)

And he made tracks, you know? And that's the reason it hit me first when I mention him, I said Bear Tracks, because you know -- and let's see, who else? We had a guy singing the blues called Blues Bailey and let me see, who else was in that band? Oh, tenor man that went on the West Coast there. What was his name? He was good. If I can think of his name.
Not Jack McVeigh.
Not McNea, but this guy did a lot of work with the recording studios.
Bumps Myers?
Not Bumps. I remember Bumps. But oh, if I called his name, you would recognize it right off. It's a shame that I can't remember. Maxwell Davis.
Oh!
Maxwell. And Maxwell was blowing great.
He could blow.

Yes, and he had some nice guys in the trumpet section, Von Slits -- some guy named Von Slits out of Texas and had two or three other good trumpet players. I didn't remember their names as well, but I would definitely remember Maxwell, because Maxwell would take those solos that, you know --
Who was on piano?
His wife, had his wife on piano. And he was on drums.
Was she any good?

Yes, she was -- she was playing right along with the band. I mean, she wasn't no Mary Lou Williams, but she did a beautiful job. I mean, she did the job, you know. Oh, and some other guys that I would like to remember out of that band, which were good musicians, you know? But
that was the first time I --
Was that the first time Howard had heard a big band, too?
